scope.case: circular Couette reference compared with the accepted true-polygon, impermeable Cut-cell solution
scope.geometry: ri=0.5 m, ro=1 m, inner speed=0.5 m/s
scope.pressure: kinematic pressure in m2/s2; area-weighted gauge removed
scope.quantiles: cell pressure-error quantiles weighted by final physical fluid area
scope.concentration: smallest set of cells whose area-weighted squared pressure error reaches the stated share
scope.wallBands: cell-centre distance from the analytic circular wall; diagnostic only, not an acceptance exclusion
scope.patchTest: product gradient and complete symmetric viscous face operator applied to affine rigid rotation on each accepted mesh; no independent flow equation is solved
scope.acceptance: No product threshold, quality gate, geometry, wall condition, or solver algorithm changed. Pointwise curved-wall pressure remains unqualified.

finestUpwindControl.interpretation: The same localization with Upwind shows that the new default face-limited-linear convection is not the cause of the peak.

findings: The growing maximum is real and remains explicitly reported, but on the finest mesh half of the area-weighted squared pressure error is carried by three cells occupying 0.01645% of fluid area.
Area-weighted L1 and 99th-percentile errors decrease strongly while the pointwise maximum grows; this is a localized curved-wall/small-cell phenomenon, not a global pressure-field deterioration.

The rotor trace is exactly impermeable to roundoff and its adjacent Cartesian velocity jump halves with each geometric refinement. The correlation is diagnostic and does not by itself prove causation.

The affine rigid-rotation patch residual stays near floating-point roundoff on all four accepted meshes, ruling out a general linear-consistency failure of the complete symmetric viscous operator. It does not qualify nonlinear or corner behaviour.

No near-wall cells are deleted from reported norms and no pointwise pressure qualification is granted. The next discriminating study is fixed-polygon spatial refinement or a polygon-consistent reference, followed by independent curved-flow regression before any product change.
